facts.statement: Korora fossils date from the Late Oligocene to the Early Miocene.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Oligocene to Early Miocene,

facts.statement: Korora was a relatively small and slender penguin, similar in size to larger crested penguins.
facts.quote: It was relatively small and slender, similar in size to one of the larger crested penguins.

facts.statement: Brian Marples described Korora in 1952 based on a tarsometatarsus fossil collected from the Hakataramea Valley in New Zealand's South Island.
facts.quote: The penguin was described by Brian Marples in 1952 from fossil material (a tarsometatarsus) he collected in the Hakataramea Valley, in the Canterbury region of the South Island.

facts.statement: The genus name Korora comes from the Māori word for the little penguin.
facts.quote: The genus name Korora is the Māori term for the extant little penguin.

facts.statement: The species name oliveri honors Walter Oliver, a former director of the Dominion Museum.
facts.quote: The specific epithet honours Walter Oliver (1883–1957) a former director of the Dominion Museum.

facts.statement: Korora belongs to the bird order Sphenisciformes.
Korora lived between 25.2 and 21.7 million years ago during the Chattian to Aquitanian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Chattian to Aquitanian (25.2 to 21.7 million years ago)
